profile.name: Jalal Ahmmed

profile.tagline: I build lightweight deep learning models for medical imaging and agriculture, and make them explain themselves.
profile.photoAlt: Portrait of Jalal Ahmmed, Graduate Researcher in Explainable AI
about: I’m **Jalal Ahmmed**, a graduate researcher in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at **Daffodil International University** in Dhaka, Bangladesh. As a research assistant in the Kabir Research Group, I design deep learning models that are small enough to run on modest hardware and transparent enough to be trusted when the stakes are high.

My work spans medical imaging (mammography, neuroimaging and leukemia), agricultural AI (medicinal plant and mango leaf disease) and educational data mining. I pair lightweight architectures (compact CNNs, CNN–Transformer hybrids and CNN–spiking neural network hybrids) with explainability methods such as Grad-CAM, SHAP and LIME, so each prediction comes with evidence that a clinician, farmer or educator can check.

I’m first author of three Q1 journal articles in *Scientific Reports* (Nature Portfolio) and *IEEE Access*, written with collaborators at Hamad Bin Khalifa University in Qatar and Mälardalen University in Sweden. I’m now preparing for graduate study in trustworthy, resource-efficient artificial intelligence.

points: Research on explainable AI and ensemble learning for medical and agricultural applications.
Designed lightweight CNN, CNN–Transformer and CNN–SNN models for mammography, neuroimaging and plant disease classification.
Built and published two open datasets on Mendeley Data.
Led model evaluation (cross-validation, ablation studies, external validation, statistical testing) and manuscript preparation for Q1 journals.
Collaborated with researchers at Hamad Bin Khalifa University (Qatar) and Mälardalen University (Sweden).
Led a local volunteer team during the 2024 floods, coordinating the distribution of food, clean water and medicine to affected families.

publications.title: LBNet: An Optimized Lightweight CNN for Mammographic Breast Cancer Classification with XAI-Based Interpretability
publications.summary: A five-layer CNN with only 2.4M trainable parameters: 97.28% accuracy on RSNA, 99.54% on CBIS-DDSM and 98.50% on MIAS, with SHAP and Grad-CAM highlighting the diagnostically relevant regions of each mammogram.

publications.title: A Lightweight Hybrid CNN and Transformer Model for Medicinal Leaf Disease Classification with Explainable AI
publications.summary: Introduces **LSeTNet**, a CNN–Transformer hybrid with squeeze-and-excitation blocks: 99.72% accuracy across 12 disease classes of Tulsi, Neem and Patharkuchi with 9.38M parameters, 99.42% on an external dataset, and Grad-CAM, LIME and t-SNE explanations.

publications.title: Fine-Tuned CNN-Based Approach for Multi-Class Mango Leaf Disease Detection
publications.summary: Compares five fine-tuned CNNs on eight mango leaf classes; DenseNet201 performs best at 99.33% accuracy.

publications.title: HPrEd: A Tuned Ensemble with Model-Agnostic XAI to Explain Social Media’s Association with Academic Productivity
publications.summary: A soft-voting ensemble of Extra Trees, k-NN and MLP reaching 98.25% recall with a 0.53% false-alarm rate. SHAP and LIME identify which social media habits are tied to lower academic productivity.

projects.name: LBSpikeNet
projects.label: B.Sc. thesis, 2025–2026. Lead researcher
projects.subtitle: A lightweight hybrid CNN–SNN framework with explainable AI for multi-brain-disease classification
projects.description: Combines convolutional feature extraction with spiking neural network layers to classify brain tumor, Alzheimer’s disease and stroke from neuroimaging. Accuracy of 99.24%, 99.30% and 98.00% on the three datasets, interpreted with Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, LIME and t-SNE.
